name: LTM4668AIY#PBF
title: LTM4668A: quad 1.2 A step-down µModule regulator, 2.7 V to 17 V in, 0.6 V to 5.5 V out, outputs parallelable to 4.8 A
summary: A complete four-channel buck regulator in a 6.25 mm × 6.25 mm × 2.1 mm, 49-ball BGA: the controllers, MOSFETs, inductors and compensation are inside, so each channel needs only input and output ceramics and one resistor to set its voltage. It runs from 2.7 V to 17 V and gives 0.6 V to 5.5 V at 1.2 A per channel, and the channels can be joined in groups for 2.4 A, 3.6 A or 4.8 A. It switches at 2.25 MHz with peak-current-mode control, can be synchronized from 1.5 MHz to 3 MHz, offers Burst Mode, pulse-skipping or forced continuous operation and 100 % duty cycle, and gives each channel its own power-good output and enable; protection covers overvoltage, overcurrent and overtemperature. It is pin compatible with the LTM4668, the 1 MHz version for 0.6 V to 1.8 V outputs.
key_figures: 1.2A per channel; up to 4.8A with all four paralleled
3.25V min, 3.35V max for 3.3V over line, load and temperature

circuits.title: 5V to 17V Input, Quad 1.5V, 1.8V, 2.5V, 3.3V Output DC/DC µModule Regulator
circuits.description: Four separate rails from one 5 V to 17 V input, each good for 1.2 A. Two 22 µF / 25 V ceramics bypass VIN, and all four RUN inputs are wired straight to VIN. Each output has one 47 µF / 6.3 V ceramic, and a single resistor from each FB pin to ground picks the voltage against the internal 60.4 kΩ: 40.2 kΩ for 1.5 V on channel 1, 19.1 kΩ for 2.5 V on channel 2, 13.3 kΩ for 3.3 V on channel 3 and 30.1 kΩ for 1.8 V on channel 4. MODE/SYNC is grounded, which selects pulse-skipping at light load. The PGOOD outputs and INTVCC have no external connection.

circuits.title: Figure 14. 6V to 17V Input, 3.3V, 2V, 5V, 1.8V Output at 1.2A Design
circuits.description: Four independent 1.2 A outputs from a 6 V to 17 V supply: 3.3 V, 2 V, 5 V and 1.8 V on channels 1 to 4, set by 13.3 kΩ, 25.5 kΩ, 8.25 kΩ and 30.1 kΩ from FB to ground. One 22 µF / 25 V ceramic sits on VIN; each output carries one 47 µF / 6.3 V ceramic. RUN1 to RUN4 are tied to VIN. MODE/SYNC goes to ground for pulse-skipping at light load. The four PGOOD flags are brought out as separate signals; INTVCC is left unconnected. The load-step results of Table 8 were measured on this circuit.

circuits.title: Figure 15. 5V to 17V Input, 1V and 3.3V Output at 2.4A Design with Pulse-Skipping Mode
circuits.description: Two rails of 2.4 A each, built as a 2+2 parallel arrangement. Channel 1 is the master of channel 2: VOUT1 and VOUT2 are joined, FB2 is tied to INTVCC, and 90.9 kΩ from FB1 to ground sets 1.0 V. Channel 4 is the master of channel 3: VOUT3 and VOUT4 are joined, FB3 is tied to INTVCC, and 13.3 kΩ from FB4 to ground sets 3.3 V. Each rail has one 47 µF / 6.3 V ceramic; VIN (5 V to 17 V) has one 22 µF / 25 V ceramic. RUN1 and RUN2 are tied to VIN, while RUN3 and RUN4 are joined to each other and form a separate enable for the 3.3 V rail. MODE/SYNC is grounded for pulse-skipping operation.

circuits.title: Figure 16. 2.7V to 17V Input, Four Phase Parallel Single Output 1.8V at 4.8A Design
circuits.description: All four channels feed one 1.8 V, 4.8 A output. Channel 1 is the master: 30.1 kΩ from FB1 to ground sets the voltage, and FB2, FB3 and FB4 are tied to INTVCC so channels 2 to 4 follow it. The four VOUT pins are joined and the output has two 47 µF / 6.3 V ceramics in parallel. All RUN inputs go to VIN, which takes 2.7 V to 17 V and has one 22 µF / 25 V ceramic. MODE/SYNC is grounded. PGOOD1 is the flag to use for this combined output.

operation.text: Four independent non-isolated buck channels share one input. Each channel is a fixed-frequency peak-current-mode regulator with its own power MOSFETs, inductor and compensation inside the package, so only input and output capacitors and one feedback resistor per channel are needed outside. Each channel's inductor is 1 µH and its upper feedback resistor 60.4 kΩ. Input range is 2.7 V to 17 V and output range 0.6 V to 5.5 V; each channel delivers 1.2 A continuous.

The channels switch at 2.25 MHz by default. A clock on MODE/SYNC between 1.5 MHz and 3 MHz (within ±50 % of 2.25 MHz) is detected and locked to by an internal PLL, which aligns every top-MOSFET turn-on with the clock's rising edge; while synchronized the module runs forced continuous. The clock needs pulses at least 400 ns wide, a high level above 2 V and a low level below 0.3 V. The PLL stays off during start-up.

MODE/SYNC at INTVCC selects Burst Mode operation: the inductor peak current is held at about 400 mA, and when the error amplifier output (COMP) falls below 0.2 V the channel stops both switches and sleeps, the output capacitor carrying the load until VOUT sags and switching resumes. With every channel asleep the module draws 8 µA from VIN. MODE/SYNC at GND selects pulse-skipping, which works the same way with a peak current of at least 66 mA, giving less ripple and slightly less efficiency than Burst Mode. Both modes change over from continuous operation by themselves as load falls. A level of INTVCC/2 on the pin (anywhere from 1 V to INTVCC - 1.2 V) selects forced continuous mode, in which inductor current may reverse at light load and the top switch fires every cycle, for fixed frequency and lowest ripple.

How low VOUT/VIN may go is bounded by the minimum on-time in forced continuous mode; below that, pulse-skipping or Burst Mode lets the channel drop its frequency and stay in regulation, and the LTM4668 (1 MHz) is the pin-compatible choice for high-VIN, low-VOUT rails. At the other end the channel can run at 100 % duty cycle: in dropout the top PMOS switch stays on and the control circuits remain active.

Each channel has a fixed internal soft-start ramp of 800 µs. During soft-start the channel runs in pulse-skipping mode whatever MODE/SYNC selects, so inductor current cannot reverse before the output reaches regulation; afterwards it moves to the selected mode.

Each channel has its own RUN input. Above 1 V the channel turns on; pulled below 0.35 V (or to ground) it shuts down with both MOSFETs and most of its control circuitry off. INTVCC starts only when at least one RUN input is high.

Each PGOOD is an open-drain output that pulls low when its FB voltage leaves a ±7.5 % window around 0.6 V. A pull-up resistor to a chosen supply makes it a logic signal. The falling edge is blanked for about 32 switching cycles so that transients and VOUT changes do not cause glitches. With paralleled channels use the master's PGOOD, and do not join PGOOD pins together.

Current-mode control limits current cycle by cycle. If the feedback voltage rises out of the regulation window the top FET is switched off and the bottom FET held on until the overvoltage is gone. Each regulator also stops switching when VIN rises above 19 V and restarts, through soft-start, once VIN falls below 18.7 V. The module has thermal shutdown. It has no internal fuse and no galvanic isolation between input and output; where needed, a slow-blow fuse rated at twice the maximum input current protects each unit.

Channels share current accurately when paralleled because of current-mode control. Channels 1 and 2 switch in phase, as do channels 3 and 4, and the two pairs are 180° apart, which suits 2+2, 3+1 and 4-channel arrangements. Channel 1 is master of channel 2 and channel 4 is master of channel 3; when three or four channels make one output, channel 1 leads. A slave has its FB tied to INTVCC, which shuts down its control circuits so the master's drive runs its switches; its VOUT and RUN are tied to the master's. Channels 2 and 3 cannot be paralleled with each other alone. Interleaving lowers input and output ripple current and multiplies the ripple frequency by the number of phases.

Feed the module from a low-AC-impedance source, placing a 4.7 µF ceramic input capacitor at each of the module's two sides to carry ripple current. A bulk capacitor, aluminium electrolytic or polymer, is needed only when long leads, traces or too little source capacitance raise the source impedance.

The internal loop is designed for low-ESR ceramic output capacitors alone; one ceramic per channel gives low ripple and good transient response. Where bulk output capacitors are added for ripple or transient spikes, a 10 pF to 15 pF phase-boost capacitor between VOUT and FB is recommended. Table 8 lists measured responses to a 0.3 A (25 %) load step for each output voltage.

The θ values in the pin configuration follow JESD51-9 and JESD51-12 and are meant for finite-element models; the derating curves are the guide for real use. Those curves start at 4.8 A with all four channels paralleled and 40 °C ambient, for 1.8 V, 3.3 V and 5 V outputs, and lower the current as ambient rises so the junction stays at or under 120 °C. The power loss curves are at room temperature; a factor of 1.3 covers the rise in MOSFET RDS(ON) and inductor DCR at 120 °C junction. The test board is 1.6 mm thick, six layers, 2 oz copper outside and 1 oz on the four inner layers, 94 mm × 100 mm.

Use wide copper for VIN, GND and the VOUT paths to cut conduction loss and heating. Put the high-frequency input and output ceramics right at the VIN, GND and VOUT balls. Run a solid ground layer under the module. Connect the top copper to the inner power planes through several vias; do not place vias in pads unless they are capped or plated over. Give the parts on signal pins their own SGND copper and join it to GND under the module. Bring the signal pins out to test points.
The package is moisture sensitive (MSL 4) and is not recommended for reflow on the second side of a board. Peak solder reflow body temperature is 260 °C.
